quickStart: For a police emergency in South Korea call 112; for fire or ambulance call 119.
For healthcare, confirm your National Health Insurance status and whether your My Number Card is registered as the health-insurance certificate or an eligibility document is available.
Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, investments, pensions, and essential liabilities.
If someone has died, contact the municipal office, health insurer, National Pension Service, financial institutions, employer, and tax office as relevant.
Keep the export encrypted. Never put RRN credentials, My Number Card PINs, e-Tax credentials, passwords, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes: This guide is general information, not legal, tax, insurance, or financial advice.

The 12-digit My Number is assigned to people with a resident record in Japan; the Individual Number Card is a separate card. Do not treat the identifier, physical card, and card PIN as interchangeable.

The Digital Agency states that new health insurance certificates stopped being issued from December 2, 2024. Existing certificates remained valid until expiry, up to December 1, 2025; current arrangements use a registered My Number Card or an insurer-issued eligibility certificate as applicable. Confirm with the insurer.
Japan's National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance have separate enrollment and benefit rules. Survivor benefits depend on contribution history and eligibility.

Inheritance tax may apply depending on the estate, heirs, residence, and other circumstances. NTA filing and payment requirements can include time limits; confirm current rules and advice for the specific estate.

Adult guardianship, voluntary guardianship, wills, and private powers of attorney have different legal effects. Confirm formal requirements with the relevant Family Court, a notary, or a qualified Japanese lawyer.
Official: My Number Card as health insurance certificate: https://www.digital.go.jp/en/policies/mynumber/faq-insurance-card/
Official: Japan pension systems and survivor benefits: https://www.nenkin.go.jp/international/english/japanese-system/index.html
Official: National Tax Agency inheritance tax: https://www.nta.go.jp/english/taxes/others/02/15001.htm
Emergency numbers: Japan National Police Agency: https://www.npa.go.jp/english/
Emergency numbers: Japan National Tourism Organization: https://www.japan.travel/en/plan/

dataAccess: Extract to a private, encrypted location and keep an untouched backup.
Share only with trusted authorised people; a family relationship alone does not grant legal access.
Store credentials in a reputable password manager with an emergency-access feature, not in this export.
securityTips: Never put My Number Card PINs, passwords, e-Tax credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in the export.
Use encrypted storage and secure channels for sensitive documents.
Review after major life events and at least annually; remove outdated copies securely.

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Japan. Confirm representative authority and current municipal, pension, court, and tax requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Japan
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow municipal death-registration instructions, identify the executor or representative, notify relevant insurers and providers, and keep a record of each action.

startHere: Follow the municipal death-registration and resident-record procedures that apply to the circumstances.
Locate the will and identify the executor; seek advice if there is no will or the estate is complex.
Contact the health insurer, Japan Pension Service, banks, employer, insurers, and tax office as relevant.
List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm authority and obligations before changing payments or distributing property.
Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use the deceased person's My Number Card PIN or online credentials.
legalFramework: Japan National Pension and Employees' Pension Insurance survivor-benefit rules.
National Tax Agency inheritance-tax and final income-tax rules.
Family Court adult guardianship procedures and relevant notarial instruments.
Bank, insurer, property, and investment-provider processes.

phases.title: Register and establish authority
phases.focus: Follow official municipal instructions, locate the will, and identify who may act.

keyActions.action: Contact the municipal office and follow current death-registration, resident-record, and insurance instructions.
keyActions.why: Required steps and documents depend on the person's residence, status, and circumstances.

keyActions.action: Find the will and confirm the executor; contact a Japanese lawyer or notary if there is no will, a dispute, or cross-border property.
keyActions.why: The representative may need formal authority before administering assets.

mustHaveDocuments: My Number and health-insurance record locations
Bank, pension, insurance, property, and liability references
criticalMistakes: Assuming next of kin automatically has authority
Treating My Number and My Number Card as the same thing
Putting card PINs or passwords in an exported record

phases.title: Notify insurers and providers
phases.focus: Notify health insurers, pension administrators, financial institutions, employers, and tax agencies.

keyActions.action: Contact the health insurer and Japan Pension Service about required notifications, current eligibility, and survivor claims.
keyActions.why: Insurance and pension arrangements depend on enrollment and contribution records.

keyActions.action: Contact banks, employers, insurers, brokers, and service providers separately; confirm their authority and document requirements.
keyActions.why: No single notification settles all private accounts and claims.

criticalMistakes: Assuming My Number Card is a health insurance certificate without registration

phases.title: Administer and finalise
phases.focus: Complete required court, tax, property, and provider procedures before final distribution.

keyActions.action: Confirm the required estate process and representative authority with the relevant Family Court, notary, or Japanese lawyer.
keyActions.why: The appropriate process depends on the will, estate, assets, and circumstances.

keyActions.action: Check inheritance tax and final income-tax requirements with the National Tax Agency or a qualified tax adviser.
keyActions.why: Tax scope and filing obligations depend on residence, heirs, estate value, and current rules.

mustHaveDocuments: Court or notarial documents if required
criticalMistakes: Relying on outdated tax thresholds or assumed deadlines
Distributing property before authority and tax obligations are checked
Using the deceased person's electronic credentials

phases.title: Review family arrangements
phases.focus: Review the surviving household's will, guardianship, pension, health-insurance, and secure-record arrangements.

keyActions.action: Review wills, voluntary guardianship contracts, family-court arrangements, care preferences, insurance, and pension records with appropriate professionals.
keyActions.why: Legal appointments and benefit nominations may become outdated after major family changes.

keyActions.action: Keep an asset and digital-account index; store credentials only in a suitable password manager.
keyActions.why: A secure index helps authorised people find records without exposing secrets.

criticalMistakes: Storing credentials in spreadsheets or PDFs

emergency.visitorInformation: Use JNTO visitor information for travel-related support; emergencies should go to 110/119.

healthInsurance.note: Check whether the My Number Card is registered as the health-insurance certificate or whether an eligibility certificate is in use.

inheritanceTax.note: Check current National Tax Agency filing rules and consult a tax professional for the estate's circumstances.

glossary.definition: The 12-digit Individual Number assigned to people with a resident record in Japan; it is distinct from the optional Individual Number Card.
An identity card that can be used for online procedures and, when registered, as a health insurance certificate under current arrangements.
Pension benefits that may be available to eligible survivors under the National Pension or Employees' Pension Insurance system.
